critical_point: A string cannot be changed in place, so an edit builds a new string from slices of the old one.
stem: A program must turn the text 'cat' into 'Cat'. Writing word[0] = 'C' stops with an error. Which reason explains this, and which fix works?
options_or_blanks: A string cannot be changed in place, so build a new string: 'C' + word[1:]
A string has no first position, so count from one: word[1] = 'C'
A string is too short to be edited, so add spaces to it first
Assignment is allowed only on numbers, so turn the text into a number
reason: Strings never change, so an edit builds a new string from slices of the old one: 'C' + word[1:] gives 'Cat'.
question: Q3
tip: A slice such as word[1:] is a new string holding the text from position 1 to the end.

critical_point: return ends the call and hands a value back; calls nest and the inner call runs first.
stem: The function below counts vowels, but its return line sits inside the loop. What changes in the result for banana, compared with the return placed after the loop?
options_or_blanks: It still prints 3: return only shows the value, and the loop goes on
It prints 0: return ends the call after the first letter b, so the later vowels are never counted
It prints 6: every letter is counted once more
It stops with an error: a return may not stand inside a loop
reason: return ends the call at once; inside the loop it runs after the first letter b, which is no vowel, so n is still 0.
question: Q4

critical_point: Using += on a list parameter changes the caller's list, while + would not.
stem: Read the program, then choose what the last line prints and the reason why the two functions act differently.
options_or_blanks: ['Zoe', 'Eda', 'Ali']: both functions change the caller's list
['Zoe']: a function can never change the list of its caller
['Zoe', 'Ali']: the second call replaces the change of the first
['Zoe', 'Eda']: += changes the list itself, while + builds a new list for the local name
reason: += changes the caller's list itself, so Eda stays; guests + [...] builds a new list that only the local name guests reaches, so Ali is lost.
question: Q5
tip: A line with += changes the existing list; a line with + and = makes a new list.

critical_point: dict.fromkeys with a list as the value gives every key the very same list.
stem: Read the program, then choose why the list of b also holds the 1 although only groups['a'] was changed.
options_or_blanks: append always adds the item to every list of a dictionary
dict.fromkeys was given one list, so every key reaches that same list
The keys a and b are equal, so they are one key
A dictionary copies a list into a key only when the key is read
reason: fromkeys uses the one object it is given as the value of every key, so a change through one key shows under all of them.
question: Q5
tip: A dictionary holds one value per key; one list given as the value is not a list per key.
